The chart has two direct callers of `reportError`, both in the orders packages. Neither is affected in a way that needs a code change beyond checking how they handle the call.

1. **`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/useOrderableConceptSets.ts`**, `useOrderableConceptSets` (lines 65–90). The `useEffect` at lines 71–75 calls `reportError(error)` when the SWR fetch fails.
2. **Same file**, the private hook `useOrderableConceptSWR` (lines 23–61). Its `useEffect` at lines 34–38 also calls `reportError(error)` on fetch failure.
3. **`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-favorites/useFavoritesActions.ts`**, `persistFavorites` inside `useFavoritesActions` (lines 25–68). The `catch` at lines 55–65 calls `reportError(error)` after a failed save.

Two more chart call sites use `createErrorHandler` from the same module, in `packages/esm-patient-notes-app/src/notes/visit-notes-form.component.tsx` (lines 251 and 566). They don't call `reportError` directly, and the handler they create is discarded without being invoked, so they are not affected. I left them out of the JSON for that reason.

In `openmrs-esm-core`, the definition is `packages/framework/esm-error-handling/src/index.ts` (lines 56–61). It wraps the error in an `Error` and rethrows it from a `setTimeout`, which the global `window.onerror` handler turns into a toast. A behaviour change there (sync vs. async throw, toast vs. console, or error normalisation) would reach the three chart call sites above. `createErrorHandler` (lines 83–90) also forwards to `reportError`, so it is the core-side path to the chart's two discarded handlers. The core's own callers (`current-user.ts`, `esm-styleguide/src/modals/index.tsx`) are outside the chart and not listed.
